messages.snippet: Rachel, Attaching our first draft of the share purchase agreement. The key liability and protection
messages.subject: Project Relay - SPA: our first draft
messages.plaintextBody:
Rachel,

Attaching our first draft of the share purchase agreement. The key liability and protection positions are:

- General warranty cap at 50 per cent. of Consideration; overall cap at 100 per cent. (clause 9.2-9.3).
- General warranty survival of 24 months; tax/fundamentals to the seventh anniversary (clause 9.6).
- De minimis per claim of GBP 25,000 and a basket (threshold) of GBP 380,000 (clause 9.4-9.5).
- Locked box off the 30 September accounts; permitted leakage limited to the customary carve-outs only (clause 4.3).
- Sellers' non-compete of 24 months and non-solicitation of 24 months (clause 12).
- A customary, unqualified Material Adverse Change condition (clause 16), no industry/economic carve-outs.
- Retention of GBP 3,800,000 (10 per cent.) into escrow for 24 months (clause 15).
- W&I: drafted on the basis a buy-side policy is being explored; limit to be confirmed.

Subject to contract and to DD. Look forward to your mark-up.

Best,
Elena

--
Whitfield Carter LLP | 22 Bishopsgate, London EC2N 4BQ
Confidential and may be legally privileged.

messages.snippet: Elena, Our formal mark-up (Draft 2) is attached. The headline movements, which our clients regard as
messages.subject: RE: Project Relay - SPA: our first draft
messages.plaintextBody:
Elena,

Our formal mark-up (Draft 2) is attached. The headline movements, which our clients regard as essential:

- General warranty cap reduced from 50 to 30 per cent. of Consideration. A 50 per cent. cap is simply too high where the sellers are rolling and a W&I policy is going on risk behind the warranties.
- General survival cut from 24 to 18 months. We will not have the sellers exposed beyond a single audit cycle.
- De minimis raised from GBP 25,000 to GBP 50,000 and the basket from GBP 380,000 to GBP 500,000.
- Sellers' non-compete cut from 24 to 12 months - 24 months is unenforceable on these facts.
- The MAC condition at clause 16 must be narrowed: it needs carve-outs for (a) general economic and market conditions, (b) conditions affecting the logistics/last-mile industry generally, and (c) changes in law, regulation or GAAP. As drafted it is far too broad and hands Bracken a walk-away.
- Permitted leakage broadened to include transaction bonuses, the sellers' and Company's adviser fees, and pre-completion tax distributions to the sellers (clause 4.3).
- We have also broadened the 'so far as the sellers are aware' knowledge qualifiers across the warranties and tightened the customer/supplier and IP wording.
- Escrow retention period reduced to match survival at 18 months.

Happy to talk these through.

Rachel

Rachel Hargrove | Partner | Hargrove & Associates LLP

messages.plaintextBody:
Rachel,

Thank you. Having taken our client's instructions, here is where we can land:

- Cap: we will come off 50 but not to 30. We will meet at 40 per cent. of Consideration, with the 100 per cent. overall cap unchanged.
- Survival: we will move to 21 months - splitting the difference and, helpfully, lining the warranty period up with the escrow retention period.
- Non-compete: 18 months. That is enforceable on these facts and we will not go to 12.
- De minimis GBP 35,000 and basket GBP 450,000 - between our positions.
- MAC: we accept carve-outs (a) general economic/market conditions and (b) industry-wide conditions. We do not accept the change-in-law/GAAP carve-out - that one comes out.
- Leakage: we accept the transaction-bonus and adviser-fee carve-outs. The pre-completion tax-distribution carve-out we cannot take.
- Knowledge qualifiers: we have reinstated the unqualified wording on the core customer/supplier and IP warranties; a limited number of 'so far as aware' qualifiers can stay where they are genuinely outside the sellers' knowledge.
- Escrow retention period moves to 21 months to track survival.

If your clients are comfortable with that package we can move to an execution draft.

Best,
Elena

--
Whitfield Carter LLP | 22 Bishopsgate, London EC2N 4BQ
Confidential and may be legally privileged.

messages.htmlBody:
Elena,

That package works for our clients. To confirm what we are accepting: 40 per cent. general cap (100 per cent. overall); 21-month general survival with the escrow period to match; 18-month non-compete (24-month non-solicit unchanged); de minimis GBP 35,000 and basket GBP 450,000; MAC with the economic and industry carve-outs only; and the transaction-bonus and adviser-fee leakage carve-outs, dropping the tax-distribution point. We will live with the reinstated knowledge qualifiers on the core warranties on the basis the W&I sits behind them.

Please turn the execution draft.

Rachel

Rachel Hargrove | Partner | Hargrove & Associates LLP


On Fri, Oct 25, 2024 at 3:15 PM, Elena Marchetti <elena.marchetti@whitfieldcarter.com> wrote:
Rachel,

Thank you. Having taken our client's instructions, here is where we can land:

- Cap: we will come off 50 but not to 30. We will meet at 40 per cent. of Consideration, with the 100 per cent. overall cap unchanged.
- Survival: we will move to 21 months - splitting the difference and, helpfully, lining the warranty period up with the escrow retention period.
- Non-compete: 18 months. That is enforceable on these facts and we will not go to 12.
- De minimis GBP 35,000 and basket GBP 450,000 - between our positions.
- MAC: we accept carve-outs (a) general economic/market conditions and (b) industry-wide conditions. We do not accept the change-in-law/GAAP carve-out - that one comes out.
- Leakage: we accept the transaction-bonus and adviser-fee carve-outs. The pre-completion tax-distribution carve-out we cannot take.
- Knowledge qualifiers: we have reinstated the unqualified wording on the core customer/supplier and IP warranties; a limited number of 'so far as aware' qualifiers can stay where they are genuinely outside the sellers' knowledge.
- Escrow retention period moves to 21 months to track survival.

If your clients are comfortable with that package we can move to an execution draft.

Best,
Elena

--
Whitfield Carter LLP | 22 Bishopsgate, London EC2N 4BQ
Confidential and may be legally privileged.


On Mon, Oct 21, 2024 at 4:50 PM, Rachel Hargrove <rachel.hargrove@hargroveassoc.com> wrote:
Elena,

Our formal mark-up (Draft 2) is attached. The headline movements, which our clients regard as essential:

- General warranty cap reduced from 50 to 30 per cent. of Consideration. A 50 per cent. cap is simply too high where the sellers are rolling and a W&I policy is going on risk behind the warranties.
- General survival cut from 24 to 18 months. We will not have the sellers exposed beyond a single audit cycle.
- De minimis raised from GBP 25,000 to GBP 50,000 and the basket from GBP 380,000 to GBP 500,000.
- Sellers' non-compete cut from 24 to 12 months - 24 months is unenforceable on these facts.
- The MAC condition at clause 16 must be narrowed: it needs carve-outs for (a) general economic and market conditions, (b) conditions affecting the logistics/last-mile industry generally, and (c) changes in law, regulation or GAAP. As drafted it is far too broad and hands Bracken a walk-away.
- Permitted leakage broadened to include transaction bonuses, the sellers' and Company's adviser fees, and pre-completion tax distributions to the sellers (clause 4.3).
- We have also broadened the 'so far as the sellers are aware' knowledge qualifiers across the warranties and tightened the customer/supplier and IP wording.
- Escrow retention period reduced to match survival at 18 months.

Happy to talk these through.

Rachel

Rachel Hargrove | Partner | Hargrove & Associates LLP

Rachel,

Attaching our first draft of the share purchase agreement. The key liability and protection positions are:

- General warranty cap at 50 per cent. of Consideration; overall cap at 100 per cent. (clause 9.2-9.3).
- General warranty survival of 24 months; tax/fundamentals to the seventh anniversary (clause 9.6).
- De minimis per claim of GBP 25,000 and a basket (threshold) of GBP 380,000 (clause 9.4-9.5).
- Locked box off the 30 September accounts; permitted leakage limited to the customary carve-outs only (clause 4.3).
- Sellers' non-compete of 24 months and non-solicitation of 24 months (clause 12).
- A customary, unqualified Material Adverse Change condition (clause 16), no industry/economic carve-outs.
- Retention of GBP 3,800,000 (10 per cent.) into escrow for 24 months (clause 15).
- W&I: drafted on the basis a buy-side policy is being explored; limit to be confirmed.

Subject to contract and to DD. Look forward to your mark-up.

Best,
Elena

--
Whitfield Carter LLP | 22 Bishopsgate, London EC2N 4BQ

Tom

On Tue, Oct 29, 2024 at 11:50 AM, Rachel Hargrove <rachel.hargrove@hargroveassoc.com> wrote:
Elena,

That package works for our clients. To confirm what we are accepting: 40 per cent. general cap (100 per cent. overall); 21-month general survival with the escrow period to match; 18-month non-compete (24-month non-solicit unchanged); de minimis GBP 35,000 and basket GBP 450,000; MAC with the economic and industry carve-outs only; and the transaction-bonus and adviser-fee leakage carve-outs, dropping the tax-distribution point. We will live with the reinstated knowledge qualifiers on the core warranties on the basis the W&I sits behind them.

Please turn the execution draft.

Rachel

Rachel Hargrove | Partner | Hargrove & Associates LLP


On Fri, Oct 25, 2024 at 3:15 PM, Elena Marchetti <elena.marchetti@whitfieldcarter.com> wrote:
Rachel,

Thank you. Having taken our client's instructions, here is where we can land:

- Cap: we will come off 50 but not to 30. We will meet at 40 per cent. of Consideration, with the 100 per cent. overall cap unchanged.
- Survival: we will move to 21 months - splitting the difference and, helpfully, lining the warranty period up with the escrow retention period.
- Non-compete: 18 months. That is enforceable on these facts and we will not go to 12.
- De minimis GBP 35,000 and basket GBP 450,000 - between our positions.
- MAC: we accept carve-outs (a) general economic/market conditions and (b) industry-wide conditions. We do not accept the change-in-law/GAAP carve-out - that one comes out.
- Leakage: we accept the transaction-bonus and adviser-fee carve-outs. The pre-completion tax-distribution carve-out we cannot take.
- Knowledge qualifiers: we have reinstated the unqualified wording on the core customer/supplier and IP warranties; a limited number of 'so far as aware' qualifiers can stay where they are genuinely outside the sellers' knowledge.
- Escrow retention period moves to 21 months to track survival.

If your clients are comfortable with that package we can move to an execution draft.

Best,
Elena

On Mon, Oct 21, 2024 at 4:50 PM, Rachel Hargrove <rachel.hargrove@hargroveassoc.com> wrote:
Elena,

Our formal mark-up (Draft 2) is attached. The headline movements, which our clients regard as essential:

- General warranty cap reduced from 50 to 30 per cent. of Consideration. A 50 per cent. cap is simply too high where the sellers are rolling and a W&I policy is going on risk behind the warranties.
- General survival cut from 24 to 18 months. We will not have the sellers exposed beyond a single audit cycle.
- De minimis raised from GBP 25,000 to GBP 50,000 and the basket from GBP 380,000 to GBP 500,000.
- Sellers' non-compete cut from 24 to 12 months - 24 months is unenforceable on these facts.
- The MAC condition at clause 16 must be narrowed: it needs carve-outs for (a) general economic and market conditions, (b) conditions affecting the logistics/last-mile industry generally, and (c) changes in law, regulation or GAAP. As drafted it is far too broad and hands Bracken a walk-away.
- Permitted leakage broadened to include transaction bonuses, the sellers' and Company's adviser fees, and pre-completion tax distributions to the sellers (clause 4.3).
- We have also broadened the 'so far as the sellers are aware' knowledge qualifiers across the warranties and tightened the customer/supplier and IP wording.
- Escrow retention period reduced to match survival at 18 months.

Happy to talk these through.

Rachel

Rachel Hargrove | Partner | Hargrove & Associates LLP
